source_batch.unit_label: Module A unit 8: EXIM Bank, Reserve Bank, FEMA, FEDAI and depositary receipts

facts.statement: EXIM Bank of India was set up in 1981 under the Export Import Bank of India Act 1981 as the principal financial institution for financing and coordinating the financing of export and import trade, especially on a long-term basis, and arranges lines of credit to other governments. Its philosophy: make exports competitive by offering finance at competitive rates, develop alternative financing, supply information and advice on export opportunities, provide selective production, marketing and financing support, and respond to exporters' problems.

EXIM Bank products, per the courseware: Buyer's Credit (a non-LC facility under which an overseas buyer can import Indian goods and services on deferred payment, and a medium- and long-term facility to foreign project companies awarding work to Indian project exporters); corporate banking (research and development finance, pre-shipment and post-shipment credit, import finance, production equipment finance, finance for special purpose vehicles of SME clusters and others); Lines of Credit to overseas financial institutions, regional development banks and governments for imports from India on deferred terms; overseas investment finance (equity finance for joint ventures abroad); project export finance (civil engineering and construction, turnkey projects, technical and consultancy services, supplies), funded and non-funded; consultancy and technology services; import loans for third-country projects; international merchant banking; the Export Marketing Fund; Product Liability Insurance cost sharing for exports to OECD countries; and the Export Vendor Development Lending Programme.

The Reserve Bank may give authorised persons directions on payments or on doing or desisting from any act relating to foreign exchange or foreign security to secure compliance with the Act, rules, regulations, notifications or directions, may direct them to furnish information, and, after giving a reasonable opportunity of being heard, may penalise an authorised person who contravenes a direction or fails to file a return directed by it with a penalty up to ten thousand rupees and, for a continuing contravention, an additional penalty up to two thousand rupees for every day it continues.

The courseware describes exchange control in India as beginning with the Defence of India Rules 1935 during the war, becoming the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1973 (in force 1 January 1974), which was repealed and replaced by the Foreign Exchange Management Act 1999, in force from 1 June 2000. FEMA's objective is to facilitate external trade and payments and promote the orderly development and maintenance of the foreign exchange market in India, whereas FERA aimed to conserve foreign exchange. Contraventions of FEMA are dealt with under civil law, while under FERA they were criminal and non-bailable. The Act's long title and section 1 record that the Act extends to the whole of India.

Returns that authorised dealers submit to the Reserve Bank, per the courseware, include the bank-wide fortnightly foreign exchange return (FETERS R-returns), the statement of balances in Nostro and Vostro accounts (BAL), statements of FCNR(B) deposits (STAT 5) and of NRE and NRO deposits (STAT 8), consolidated non-resident deposit data (NRD-CSR), quarterly International Banking Statistics, the monthly statement of remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, the monthly statement of trade credit, daily data on dealing room operations (FEMIS) and Form ECB 2 for external commercial borrowings. Returns are submitted electronically.

Under the Current Account Transactions Rules the drawal of foreign exchange (including opening a letter of credit or using an international credit, debit or ATM card) is prohibited for transactions in Schedule I, for travel to Nepal or Bhutan, and for transactions with a person resident in Nepal or Bhutan (the last may be exempted by the Reserve Bank). Schedule I lists: remittance out of lottery winnings; remittance of income from racing, riding or any other hobby; remittance for purchase of lottery tickets, banned magazines, football pools or sweepstakes; payment of commission on exports towards equity investment in joint ventures or wholly owned subsidiaries abroad; remittance of dividend by a company to which dividend balancing applies; payment of commission on exports under the Rupee State Credit Route (except up to 10 per cent of invoice value for tea and tobacco); payment for call back services of telephones; and remittance of interest income on funds in the Non-Resident Special Rupee Account Scheme.

Schedule II of the Rules lists transactions needing the prior approval of the Central Government, including cultural tours (Ministry of Human Resource Development), advertisement in foreign print media by a State Government or its public sector undertakings above USD 10,000 (Ministry of Finance), freight of a vessel chartered by a public sector undertaking and import on a c.i.f. basis by a Government department or undertaking through ocean transport (Ministry of Surface Transport), hiring of transponders (Ministries of Information and Broadcasting, and of Communication and Information Technology), container detention charges above the rate fixed by the Director General of Shipping, prize money or sponsorship by non-sports bodies above USD 100,000 (Department of Youth Affairs and Sports) and membership of a P and I Club (Ministry of Finance, Insurance Division). The prior approval requirement does not apply where payment is made out of an Resident Foreign Currency account, and Rules 4 and 5 do not apply to drawal out of an EEFC account except for specified items.

Schedule III of the Rules allows individuals to draw foreign exchange within USD 250,000 per financial year for private visits (except to Nepal and Bhutan), gift or donation, going abroad for employment, emigration, maintenance of close relatives abroad, travel for business or conferences or medical check-up, medical treatment, studies abroad and any other current account transaction; amounts above the limit need the Reserve Bank's prior approval, but for emigration, medical treatment and studies a larger amount may be remitted where the country of emigration, the medical institute or the university requires it. The limit is reduced by any amount remitted under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme in the year. Persons other than individuals need the Reserve Bank's prior approval for donations above the lower of one per cent of foreign exchange earnings in the previous three years and USD 5 million for specified endowments, for commission to agents abroad for sale of flats or plots above the higher of USD 25,000 and five per cent of the inward remittance, for consultancy above USD 10 million per project for infrastructure and USD 1 million per project otherwise, and for reimbursement of pre-incorporation expenses above the higher of five per cent of investment brought in and USD 100,000.

FEDAI (Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India) was formed in August 1958 with the approval of the Reserve Bank to take over certain functions of the Exchange Banks' Association; it is a self-regulatory organisation of banks authorised to deal in foreign exchange, incorporated under Section 25 of the Companies Act 1956. Its functions include issuing guidelines and rules for foreign exchange business, training bank personnel, accrediting forex brokers, advising member banks on dealing issues, representing members before the Government and the Reserve Bank, and announcing periodical rates such as foreign exchange revaluation rates (some now advised by Financial Benchmarks India Pvt Ltd). The courseware says its rules (10th edition) were updated to 15 November 2020 and consist of eight rules; the rules saved for this course are the 10th edition as updated on 5 April 2024.

facts.statement: An American Depositary Receipt (ADR) is a certificate issued by a US bank representing shares of a foreign company, traded in the US like local shares; a depositary bank sets the ratio of ADRs to home-country shares. Unsponsored ADRs are set up by brokers without the company's formal arrangement (traded over the counter, often several depositary banks); sponsored ADRs are promoted by the company with one depositary bank, and the company bears the costs and gets the proceeds. Sponsored ADRs come in three levels: Level 1 (over-the-counter, least requirements), Level 2 (listed on an exchange, more requirements) and Level 3 (a public offering of ADRs on a US exchange to raise capital). A Global Depositary Receipt (GDR) is a certificate issued in more than one country for shares of a foreign company, held by a foreign branch of an international bank, traded across several markets (mainly European) and denominated in dollars or euros; a GDR called EDR when in euros; a GDR holder may sell it, convert it into the underlying shares or cancel it.

Foreign currency convertible bonds (FCCBs) are bonds issued in a foreign currency that may be converted into equity shares or depository receipts of the issuer at a predetermined price or rate after a period, and appear as a liability until converted; foreign currency exchangeable bonds (FCEBs), introduced by the scheme of 15 February 2008, are bonds issued by an Indian company in foreign currency that are exchangeable into the equity shares of another listed group company (the offered company). Under the February 2026 Borrowing and Lending Regulations, conversion of an ECB (including an FCCB and an FCEB) into non-debt instruments is allowed subject to conditions and does not require the minimum average maturity period to be met. The courseware's conditions of a five-year minimum maturity, issue expenses ceilings and approval route for FCEBs belong to the earlier framework and are not taught.

payload.title: EXIM Bank: what it is and what it lends for
payload.core_explanation_md:
**EXIM Bank of India**, created by the **Export Import Bank of India Act, 1981**, began work in **1981** and is the **principal financial institution** for **financing export and import trade and coordinating such finance**, especially **long-term**. It also arranges **lines of credit to other governments**.

**Its aims**: competitive export finance, new ways of financing, **information and advice** on export openings, selective support for production and marketing, and help with exporters' problems.

**Products**
- **Buyer's Credit**: a **non-LC** facility letting a foreign buyer import Indian goods on **deferred payment**; also **medium and long term** credit to a foreign project company that gives a contract to an Indian project exporter.
- **Corporate banking**: R&D finance, **pre- and post-shipment credit**, import finance, production equipment finance, finance for **SPVs of SME clusters**.
- **Lines of Credit** extended to **governments, regional development banks and financial institutions abroad** so that they can import from India on **deferred terms**.
- **Overseas investment finance**: **equity finance** for joint ventures abroad.
- **Project exports**: civil construction, **turnkey**, technical and consultancy services, supplies; **funded and non-funded**.
- **Others**: import loans for third-country projects, merchant banking, **Export Marketing Fund**, **Product Liability Insurance** cost sharing (exports to **OECD** countries), **Export Vendor Development Lending Programme**.

payload.title: The Reserve Bank's powers over authorised dealers under FEMA
payload.core_explanation_md:
Under **section 11 of FEMA** the Reserve Bank may:

1. **Direct** authorised persons on **payments** or on doing or **desisting from any act** relating to foreign exchange or foreign security, to secure compliance with the Act, rules, regulations and notifications.
2. **Require information** from them in the manner it chooses.
3. **Penalise** an authorised person who **breaks a direction** or **fails to file a directed return**, after **a reasonable opportunity of being heard**: **up to ₹10,000**, and for a continuing breach **up to ₹2,000 for each day** it continues.

**Why returns matter**: the Reserve Bank compiles national data on trade, forex flows, non-resident deposits and international assets and liabilities from what dealers report, so **late, wrong or missing returns** can attract penalties.

payload.core_explanation_md:
| Return | What it reports |
| --- | --- |
| **FETERS (R returns)** | bank-wide **fortnightly** foreign exchange operations |
| **BAL** | balances in **Nostro and Vostro** accounts |
| **STAT 5** | **FCNR(B)** deposits |
| **STAT 8** | **NRE and NRO** deposits |
| **NRD-CSR** | consolidated **non-resident deposit** data |
| **IBS** | **quarterly** international assets and liabilities |
| **LRS statement** | **monthly** remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme |
| **Trade credit statement** | **monthly** buyer's and supplier's credit |

All returns are now filed **electronically**. (Source: the courseware; the list changes as the Reserve Bank retires or merges returns.)

payload.title: From FERA to FEMA
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Timeline**: **Defence of India Rules 1935** (wartime exchange control) → **FERA 1973**, in force **1 January 1974** → **FEMA 1999**, in force **1 June 2000** (FERA repealed).

**Spirit**: **FERA** aimed to **conserve** foreign exchange; **FEMA** aims to **facilitate external trade and payments** and promote **orderly development and maintenance of the foreign exchange market**.

**Law**: contraventions of **FEMA** are **civil**; under **FERA** they were **criminal and non-bailable**.

payload.title: Transactions banned outright for foreign exchange (Schedule I) and the Nepal and Bhutan rule
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Drawal of foreign exchange** (including **opening an LC or using an international card**) is **prohibited** for:

- a **Schedule I** transaction;
- **travel to Nepal or Bhutan**;
- a **transaction with a resident of Nepal or Bhutan** (RBI may exempt).

**Schedule I**
1. **Lottery winnings** remitted out.
2. Income from **racing, riding or any hobby**.
3. Buying **lottery tickets, banned magazines, football pools, sweepstakes**.
4. **Commission on exports** paid towards **equity in JVs or wholly owned subsidiaries abroad**.
5. **Dividend** by a company subject to **dividend balancing**.
6. **Commission on exports under the Rupee State Credit Route** (except up to **10%** of invoice value for **tea and tobacco**).
7. **Call back services** of telephones.
8. **Interest** on funds in the **Non-Resident Special Rupee Account** scheme.

payload.title: Schedules II and III: Government approval, and the individual and company limits
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Schedule II: prior approval of the Central Government** (not needed if paid from an **RFC account**; EEFC drawal is exempt except for specified items). Examples:

| Purpose | Approving ministry |
| --- | --- |
| **Cultural tours** | Human Resource Development |
| **State Government/PSU foreign print advertising** above **USD 10,000** | Finance (Economic Affairs) |
| **Freight of a vessel chartered by a PSU**; **c.i.f. ocean imports** by a Government department or PSU | Surface Transport |
| **Transponder hire** | Information and Broadcasting; Communication and IT |
| **Container detention charges** above the prescribed rate | Surface Transport (Director General of Shipping) |
| **Prize money or sponsorship** above **USD 100,000** (non-sports bodies) | Youth Affairs and Sports |
| **P and I Club membership** | Finance (Insurance) |

**Schedule III: individuals**: up to **USD 250,000 a year** for private visits, gifts and donations, employment abroad, emigration, maintenance of close relatives, business or medical travel, treatment, studies, other current account transactions. **More needs RBI approval**, except that for **emigration, medical treatment and studies** a **larger amount** may go if the **country, hospital or university requires it**. The limit is **reduced by anything remitted under LRS** in the year.

**Schedule III: persons other than individuals** need **RBI approval** for donations above the **lower of 1% of the previous three years' foreign exchange earnings and USD 5 million**; agents' commission on **sale of flats or plots** above the **higher of USD 25,000 and 5% of the inward remittance**; **consultancy** above **USD 10 million per infrastructure project** or **USD 1 million per other project**; **pre-incorporation expenses** above the **higher of 5% of investment and USD 100,000**.

payload.title: FEDAI: who it is and what it does
payload.core_explanation_md:
**FEDAI** was formed in **August 1958**, with **Reserve Bank approval**, to take over some functions of the **Exchange Banks' Association**. It is a **self-regulatory organisation** of banks that deal in foreign exchange, a company under **Section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956**.

**Functions**: frame **guidelines and rules** for forex business; **train** bank staff; **accredit forex brokers**; **advise** member banks; **represent** them to the Government and the RBI; announce **periodical rates** (such as **revaluation rates**; some now come from **Financial Benchmarks India Pvt Ltd**).

**Rules**: the book cites the **10th edition updated to 15 November 2020** with **eight rules**; the edition used elsewhere in this course is the **version updated on 5 April 2024**.

payload.title: ADRs and GDRs: how they differ
payload.core_explanation_md:
**ADR**: a certificate issued by a **US bank** for shares of a **foreign company**, traded in the US like local shares; the **depositary bank sets the ratio** of ADRs to shares.

| Type | Who sets it up | Costs and proceeds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Unsponsored** | **brokers**, with no formal arrangement; **over the counter**; may have several depositary banks | company is not involved |
| **Sponsored** | the **company**, with **one depositary bank** | **company bears costs and gets proceeds** |

**Sponsored levels**: **Level 1** over the counter, **fewest requirements**; **Level 2** **listed on an exchange**; **Level 3** a **public offering** on a US exchange to **raise capital**.

**GDR**: a certificate issued in **more than one country** for shares of a foreign company, held by a **foreign branch of an international bank**, traded across markets (mainly **Europe**), in **dollars or euros** (an **EDR** when in euros). A holder can **sell it, convert it into the shares, or cancel it**.

payload.title: FCCBs and FCEBs
payload.core_explanation_md:
**FCCB**: a bond issued in a **foreign currency** that can be **converted into equity shares or depository receipts of the issuer** at a **preset price or rate** after a period; until then it is a **liability**.

**FCEB**: a foreign currency bond issued by an **Indian company** that can be **exchanged into shares of another listed group company** (the **offered company**), under the scheme of **15 February 2008**.

**Today**: under the **February 2026 Borrowing and Lending Regulations**, **conversion of an ECB, including an FCCB or FCEB, into non-debt instruments** is allowed on conditions and **the minimum average maturity need not be met**. The **older five-year minimum maturity and issue-cost ceilings** in the courseware belong to the earlier framework and are not tested.

items.title: EXIM Bank: what it is and what it lends for
items.core_explanation_md:
**EXIM Bank of India**, created by the **Export Import Bank of India Act, 1981**, began work in **1981** and is the **principal financial institution** for **financing export and import trade and coordinating such finance**, especially **long-term**. It also arranges **lines of credit to other governments**.

**Its aims**: competitive export finance, new ways of financing, **information and advice** on export openings, selective support for production and marketing, and help with exporters' problems.

**Products**
- **Buyer's Credit**: a **non-LC** facility letting a foreign buyer import Indian goods on **deferred payment**; also **medium and long term** credit to a foreign project company that gives a contract to an Indian project exporter.
- **Corporate banking**: R&D finance, **pre- and post-shipment credit**, import finance, production equipment finance, finance for **SPVs of SME clusters**.
- **Lines of Credit** extended to **governments, regional development banks and financial institutions abroad** so that they can import from India on **deferred terms**.
- **Overseas investment finance**: **equity finance** for joint ventures abroad.
- **Project exports**: civil construction, **turnkey**, technical and consultancy services, supplies; **funded and non-funded**.
- **Others**: import loans for third-country projects, merchant banking, **Export Marketing Fund**, **Product Liability Insurance** cost sharing (exports to **OECD** countries), **Export Vendor Development Lending Programme**.

items.title: The Reserve Bank's powers over authorised dealers under FEMA
items.core_explanation_md:
Under **section 11 of FEMA** the Reserve Bank may:

1. **Direct** authorised persons on **payments** or on doing or **desisting from any act** relating to foreign exchange or foreign security, to secure compliance with the Act, rules, regulations and notifications.
2. **Require information** from them in the manner it chooses.
3. **Penalise** an authorised person who **breaks a direction** or **fails to file a directed return**, after **a reasonable opportunity of being heard**: **up to ₹10,000**, and for a continuing breach **up to ₹2,000 for each day** it continues.

**Why returns matter**: the Reserve Bank compiles national data on trade, forex flows, non-resident deposits and international assets and liabilities from what dealers report, so **late, wrong or missing returns** can attract penalties.

items.title: From FERA to FEMA
items.core_explanation_md:
**Timeline**: **Defence of India Rules 1935** (wartime exchange control) → **FERA 1973**, in force **1 January 1974** → **FEMA 1999**, in force **1 June 2000** (FERA repealed).

**Spirit**: **FERA** aimed to **conserve** foreign exchange; **FEMA** aims to **facilitate external trade and payments** and promote **orderly development and maintenance of the foreign exchange market**.

**Law**: contraventions of **FEMA** are **civil**; under **FERA** they were **criminal and non-bailable**.

items.title: Transactions banned outright for foreign exchange (Schedule I) and the Nepal and Bhutan rule
items.core_explanation_md:
**Drawal of foreign exchange** (including **opening an LC or using an international card**) is **prohibited** for:

- a **Schedule I** transaction;
- **travel to Nepal or Bhutan**;
- a **transaction with a resident of Nepal or Bhutan** (RBI may exempt).

**Schedule I**
1. **Lottery winnings** remitted out.
2. Income from **racing, riding or any hobby**.
3. Buying **lottery tickets, banned magazines, football pools, sweepstakes**.
4. **Commission on exports** paid towards **equity in JVs or wholly owned subsidiaries abroad**.
5. **Dividend** by a company subject to **dividend balancing**.
6. **Commission on exports under the Rupee State Credit Route** (except up to **10%** of invoice value for **tea and tobacco**).
7. **Call back services** of telephones.
8. **Interest** on funds in the **Non-Resident Special Rupee Account** scheme.

items.title: Schedules II and III: Government approval, and the individual and company limits
items.core_explanation_md:
**Schedule II: prior approval of the Central Government** (not needed if paid from an **RFC account**; EEFC drawal is exempt except for specified items). Examples:

| Purpose | Approving ministry |
| --- | --- |
| **Cultural tours** | Human Resource Development |
| **State Government/PSU foreign print advertising** above **USD 10,000** | Finance (Economic Affairs) |
| **Freight of a vessel chartered by a PSU**; **c.i.f. ocean imports** by a Government department or PSU | Surface Transport |
| **Transponder hire** | Information and Broadcasting; Communication and IT |
| **Container detention charges** above the prescribed rate | Surface Transport (Director General of Shipping) |
| **Prize money or sponsorship** above **USD 100,000** (non-sports bodies) | Youth Affairs and Sports |
| **P and I Club membership** | Finance (Insurance) |

**Schedule III: individuals**: up to **USD 250,000 a year** for private visits, gifts and donations, employment abroad, emigration, maintenance of close relatives, business or medical travel, treatment, studies, other current account transactions. **More needs RBI approval**, except that for **emigration, medical treatment and studies** a **larger amount** may go if the **country, hospital or university requires it**. The limit is **reduced by anything remitted under LRS** in the year.

**Schedule III: persons other than individuals** need **RBI approval** for donations above the **lower of 1% of the previous three years' foreign exchange earnings and USD 5 million**; agents' commission on **sale of flats or plots** above the **higher of USD 25,000 and 5% of the inward remittance**; **consultancy** above **USD 10 million per infrastructure project** or **USD 1 million per other project**; **pre-incorporation expenses** above the **higher of 5% of investment and USD 100,000**.

items.title: FEDAI: who it is and what it does
items.core_explanation_md:
**FEDAI** was formed in **August 1958**, with **Reserve Bank approval**, to take over some functions of the **Exchange Banks' Association**. It is a **self-regulatory organisation** of banks that deal in foreign exchange, a company under **Section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956**.

**Functions**: frame **guidelines and rules** for forex business; **train** bank staff; **accredit forex brokers**; **advise** member banks; **represent** them to the Government and the RBI; announce **periodical rates** (such as **revaluation rates**; some now come from **Financial Benchmarks India Pvt Ltd**).

**Rules**: the book cites the **10th edition updated to 15 November 2020** with **eight rules**; the edition used elsewhere in this course is the **version updated on 5 April 2024**.

items.title: ADRs and GDRs: how they differ
items.core_explanation_md:
**ADR**: a certificate issued by a **US bank** for shares of a **foreign company**, traded in the US like local shares; the **depositary bank sets the ratio** of ADRs to shares.

| Type | Who sets it up | Costs and proceeds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Unsponsored** | **brokers**, with no formal arrangement; **over the counter**; may have several depositary banks | company is not involved |
| **Sponsored** | the **company**, with **one depositary bank** | **company bears costs and gets proceeds** |

**Sponsored levels**: **Level 1** over the counter, **fewest requirements**; **Level 2** **listed on an exchange**; **Level 3** a **public offering** on a US exchange to **raise capital**.

**GDR**: a certificate issued in **more than one country** for shares of a foreign company, held by a **foreign branch of an international bank**, traded across markets (mainly **Europe**), in **dollars or euros** (an **EDR** when in euros). A holder can **sell it, convert it into the shares, or cancel it**.

items.title: FCCBs and FCEBs
items.core_explanation_md:
**FCCB**: a bond issued in a **foreign currency** that can be **converted into equity shares or depository receipts of the issuer** at a **preset price or rate** after a period; until then it is a **liability**.

**FCEB**: a foreign currency bond issued by an **Indian company** that can be **exchanged into shares of another listed group company** (the **offered company**), under the scheme of **15 February 2008**.

**Today**: under the **February 2026 Borrowing and Lending Regulations**, **conversion of an ECB, including an FCCB or FCEB, into non-debt instruments** is allowed on conditions and **the minimum average maturity need not be met**. The **older five-year minimum maturity and issue-cost ceilings** in the courseware belong to the earlier framework and are not tested.
